content.prompt: Solve for $\theta\in[0^{\circ},360^{\circ})$. Answer to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2\sin\theta-1&=0\\\sin\theta&=\frac12\\A&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Sine is positive in Q1 and Q2.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=30^{\circ},\ 180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\\theta&=30^{\circ},150^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\sqrt2\cos\theta-1&=0\\\cos\theta&=\frac1{\sqrt2}\\A&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)=45^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Cosine is positive in Q1 and Q4.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=45^{\circ},\ 360^{\circ}-45^{\circ}\\\theta&=45^{\circ},315^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\sqrt3\tan\theta-2&=-1\\\sqrt3\tan\theta&=1\\\tan\theta&=\frac1{\sqrt3}\\A&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Tangent is positive in Q1 and Q3.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=30^{\circ},\ 180^{\circ}+30^{\circ}\\\theta&=30^{\circ},210^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}2\cos\theta+\sqrt3&=0\\\cos\theta&=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\A&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Cosine is negative in Q2 and Q3.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ},\ 180^{\circ}+30^{\circ}\\\theta&=150^{\circ},210^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}6\sin\theta+3&=0\\\sin\theta&=-\frac12\\A&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac12\right)=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Sine is negative in Q3 and Q4.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}+30^{\circ},\ 360^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\\theta&=210^{\circ},330^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}1+\tan\theta&=0\\\tan\theta&=-1\\A&=\tan^{-1}(1)=45^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Tangent is negative in Q2 and Q4.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ},\ 360^{\circ}-45^{\circ}\\\theta&=135^{\circ},315^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}2\cos^2\theta-\cos\theta&=0\\\cos\theta(2\cos\theta-1)&=0\\\cos\theta&=0\quad\text{or}\quad\frac12\end{align*}$$
For $\cos\theta=0$, $\theta=90^{\circ},270^{\circ}$.
For $\cos\theta=\frac12$, the reference angle is $A=\cos^{-1}(\frac12)=60^{\circ}$; cosine is positive in Q1 and Q4.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=60^{\circ},\ 360^{\circ}-60^{\circ}\\\theta&=60^{\circ},300^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
All solutions are $60^{\circ},90^{\circ},270^{\circ},300^{\circ}$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan^2\theta&=\tan\theta\\\tan^2\theta-\tan\theta&=0\\\tan\theta(\tan\theta-1)&=0\\\tan\theta&=0\quad\text{or}\quad1\end{align*}$$
For $\tan\theta=0$, $\theta=0^{\circ},180^{\circ}$.
For $\tan\theta=1$, $A=\tan^{-1}(1)=45^{\circ}$; tangent is positive in Q1 and Q3.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=45^{\circ},\ 180^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\\\theta&=45^{\circ},225^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
All solutions are $0^{\circ},45^{\circ},180^{\circ},225^{\circ}$.

$$\begin{align*}\cos^2\theta&=\frac34\\\cos\theta&=\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\A&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The positive ratio gives Q1 and Q4; the negative ratio gives Q2 and Q3.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=30^{\circ},\ 180^{\circ}-30^{\circ},\\&\phantom{=}180^{\circ}+30^{\circ},\ 360^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\\theta&=30^{\circ},150^{\circ},210^{\circ},330^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\tan^2\theta&=3\\\tan\theta&=\pm\sqrt3\\A&=\tan^{-1}(\sqrt3)=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The positive ratio gives Q1 and Q3; the negative ratio gives Q2 and Q4.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=60^{\circ},\ 180^{\circ}-60^{\circ},\\&\phantom{=}180^{\circ}+60^{\circ},\ 360^{\circ}-60^{\circ}\\\theta&=60^{\circ},120^{\circ},240^{\circ},300^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}2\cos^2\theta-1&=0\\\cos^2\theta&=\frac12\\\cos\theta&=\pm\frac1{\sqrt2}\\A&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)=45^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The positive ratio gives Q1 and Q4; the negative ratio gives Q2 and Q3.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=45^{\circ},\ 180^{\circ}-45^{\circ},\\&\phantom{=}180^{\circ}+45^{\circ},\ 360^{\circ}-45^{\circ}\\\theta&=45^{\circ},135^{\circ},225^{\circ},315^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}3\tan^2\theta-1&=0\\\tan^2\theta&=\frac13\\\tan\theta&=\pm\frac1{\sqrt3}\\A&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The positive ratio gives Q1 and Q3; the negative ratio gives Q2 and Q4.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=30^{\circ},\ 180^{\circ}-30^{\circ},\\&\phantom{=}180^{\circ}+30^{\circ},\ 360^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\\theta&=30^{\circ},150^{\circ},210^{\circ},330^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}(2\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+1)&=0\\2\sin\theta-1&=0\quad\text{or}\\\sin\theta+1&=0\\\sin\theta&=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad-1\end{align*}$$
For $\sin\theta=\frac12$, $A=\sin^{-1}(\frac12)=30^{\circ}$; sine is positive in Q1 and Q2, giving $30^{\circ},150^{\circ}$.
For $\sin\theta=-1$, $\theta=270^{\circ}$.
Thus $\theta=30^{\circ},150^{\circ},270^{\circ}$.

$$\begin{align*}2\sin^2\theta-3\sin\theta+1&=0\\(2\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta-1)&=0\\2\sin\theta-1&=0\quad\text{or}\\\sin\theta-1&=0\\\sin\theta&=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad1\end{align*}$$
For $\sin\theta=\frac12$, $A=\sin^{-1}(\frac12)=30^{\circ}$; sine is positive in Q1 and Q2, giving $30^{\circ},150^{\circ}$.
For $\sin\theta=1$, $\theta=90^{\circ}$.
Thus $\theta=30^{\circ},90^{\circ},150^{\circ}$.

answer.short: $0^{\circ},120^{\circ},240^{\circ}$. Multiply by $\cos^2\theta$ and factor; $360^{\circ}$ is excluded.
answer.worked:
Require $\cos\theta\ne0$. Multiplying by $\cos^2\theta$ gives
$$\begin{align*}1+\cos\theta-2\cos^2\theta&=0\\2\cos^2\theta-\cos\theta-1&=0\\(2\cos\theta+1)(\cos\theta-1)&=0\\2\cos\theta+1&=0\quad\text{or}\\\cos\theta-1&=0\\\cos\theta&=-\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad1\end{align*}$$
For $\cos\theta=-\frac12$, $A=\cos^{-1}(\frac12)=60^{\circ}$; cosine is negative in Q2 and Q3, giving $120^{\circ},240^{\circ}$.
For $\cos\theta=1$, $\theta=0^{\circ}$ within the interval; $360^{\circ}$ is excluded.
Thus $\theta=0^{\circ},120^{\circ},240^{\circ}$.
